title: Final pay and the separation checklist
summary: The next-regular-payday rule, when commissions and bonuses fall due, what may come out of the last check, and the notices that follow a separation.

blocks.text: An employee whose employment ends for any reason must be paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday, through the regular pay channels or by trackable mail if the employee requests that in writing. Wages based on bonuses, commissions or other calculations are due on the first regular payday after the amount becomes calculable. Those amounts may be forfeited only if the employee was notified, under G.S. 95-25.13, of the policy or practice that produces the forfeiture; an employee who was not notified is not subject to it. The employer does not choose the timeline and may not hold the check pending return of property or signature of a release.

Where wages are in dispute, the employer must pay the undisputed portion on time and without condition, and any release demanded as a condition of partial payment is void. Deductions from the final check follow the same rules as any other paycheck under G.S. 95-25.8, with one relaxation: the seven-day advance notice for cash or inventory shortage or property damage is not required when a separation occurs. Every other element still applies, including the signed authorization, the advance written notice of the amount, the right to withdraw, and the bar on touching overtime wages.

items: Severance is a wage under G.S. 95-25.2(16) when the employer has a policy or practice of paying it; a severance agreement that pays extra in exchange for a release is lawful because the release is not a condition of wages already earned.
A final paycheck mailed at the employee's written request must go by trackable mail (G.S. 95-25.7).
Report separation pay, vacation payout and bonuses in the response to the Division of Employment Security; they can affect the claimant's benefits.
Unpaid final wages carry interest, an equal amount as liquidated damages absent proof of good faith, and attorneys' fees (G.S. 95-25.22).

blocks.text: The common mistake is holding the final paycheck until the laptop comes back or the separation agreement is signed. G.S. 95-25.7 sets the deadline at the next regular payday with no exception for property or paperwork, G.S. 95-25.7A voids a release demanded as a condition of payment, and a deduction for the laptop without a compliant G.S. 95-25.8 authorization is itself an unpaid wage. The employer's remedy for the laptop is a civil claim, which G.S. 95-25.8(g) preserves.
This is training, not legal advice.
